thread:
incident-bot: PagerDuty: Triggered alert: conn-errors-spike (service: inference-router) — page fired to eng-oncall
maya: acked via PD, taking lead 
pd-bot: Incident 78901 acknowledged by maya
liam: seeing alert in grafana https://grafana.redwood.example/d/ef12/inference-router 3: p99 connections jumped, error rate small spike
maya: jumping into logs, any recent deploys? infra-bot: Canary rollout inference-router@v2.7 started 45s ago
rachel: yep saw the canary, traffic-splitting 10% -> 30% over 2m, maybe the ramp overshot
liam: logs show a flood of ECONNRESET to kv-cache, e.g.: 
```
2026-11-02T03:12:10Z router-1 ERROR dial tcp 10.2.4.7:1234: i/o timeout
2026-11-02T03:12:10Z router-1 WARN retrying request (1/3)
```
maya: curious that retries are piling. Could be connection pool exhaustion during rollout. quick mitigation: pausing canary and scale up router pods
maya: `kubectl rollout pause deploy/inference-router -n prod`
liam: pausing... done. scaling to 10 replicas: `kubectl scale deploy inference-router --replicas=10 -n prod`
infra-bot: HorizontalPodAutoscaler target CPU = 60% currently, will respect manual scale
rachel: adding client-side backoff temporarily by flipping feature-flag `router-backoff=on` in configmap to reduce retries
liam: updated configmap, reloaded via `kubectl rollout restart deploy/inference-router -n prod` — new pods coming up
maya: monitoring kv-cache metrics: cold misses spiking, likely new pods warming and opening new connections to backend which caused transient saturation
liam: I can warm up kv-cache connections on new pods: 
`for p in $(kubectl get pods -l app=inference-router -o name -n prod); do kubectl exec $p -n prod -- /usr/local/bin/kv-warm --parallel 50; done`
rachel: running that now on healthy pods only
(45s pass)
liam: grafana p99 connection errors falling back toward baseline, p95 latency recovering
pd-bot: Alert auto-resolved (conn-errors-spike) 3s after trigger
maya: checking Sentry: no increase in 5xx errors, sampling of customer traces looks ok. marking as no-customer-impact for now
tom: good catch. opening follow-up ticket INFRA-482: canary-conn-pool-tuning and adding warmup hook to rollout pipeline https://redwood.atlassian.net/browse/INFRA-482
rachel: will add a safety gate to slow ramp to 5% increments and run warmup job during rollout PR
liam: also going to raise HPA minReplicas to 4 to avoid cold-start churn 
maya: note for postmortem: correlate rollout ramp rate + connection churn + kv-cache pool sizing. recommend adding runbook steps for on-call
tom: assigned, will draft runbook + small playbook snippet for quick-scale and warmup commands
maya: thumbs up. thanks team :thumbsup:
